fields.why: Weighting jurisdiction weekly medians by reinfection counts is a pooling average that only sums jurisdictions, not survey weights, IPTW, raking or poststratification; A itself offers 'other/aggregation' as an alternative and wrongly calls it primary. Rule needed: count-weighted pooling of jurisdiction summaries is arithmetic, not a procedure.

Same issue as procedure_classes: 'estimated by weighting reported weekly medians using the number of weekly reinfections per jurisdiction' is aggregation, not weighting to adjust or to reach a population.

Text and Table report all five variant periods (2.7%, 10.3%, 12.5%, 20.6%, 28.8%) and three age groups, so group fits best; B's pair reflects the headline Delta vs BQ.1/BQ.1.1 endpoint contrast, which is defensible.

The analyzed records are weekly counts reported by 18 jurisdictions' surveillance; hospital records and vital records are how the jurisdictions ascertained outcomes (footnotes), not records analyzed here. Rule needed, analogous to 'jurisdictions feeding a national system': do not list upstream ascertainment sources of a surveillance system.

'Later eligibility for vaccination' is a policy and so could count as a political determinant, but it is one of a list of infection-history and exposure explanations for an age contrast not framed as social position; false is preferred.

brief_issues: Brief does not say whether count-weighted pooling of jurisdiction summaries is a weighting procedure, or whether ascertainment sources behind a surveillance system (vital records, hospital records) are listed as data sources.
